title: E0048: Unbounded direct recursion
plain_english: This rule reports direct recursion that reuses unchanged arguments and does not reassign the corresponding parameters. These calls are strong candidates for infinite recursion.
why_matters: A recursive call that keeps the same inputs can repeat forever, leading to stack exhaustion or a process crash. Making the termination condition and the changing argument explicit helps ensure the recursion makes progress.
bad_example:
<?php
function walk(Node $node): void
{
    walk($node->next); // no base case/guard
}
good_example:
<?php
function walk(?Node $node): void
{
    if ($node === null) {
        return;
    }

    walk($node->next);
}
what_it_checks: A function calling itself with the same parameter variables
A method calling `$this->sameMethod()` with the same parameter variables
A static method calling `self::sameMethod()`, `static::sameMethod()`, or `ClassName::sameMethod()` with the same parameter variables
Zero-argument functions and methods that call themselves
